Cyber Attack Disrupts Bhutan Electric Utilities Firms’ IT Systems

Thimphu, June 17 — A cyber attack targeting IT systems of firms in Bhutan’s electric utilities industry has caused widespread disruptions, with officials warning that restoration efforts are ongoing and the full impact is still being assessed.

Bhutan Power Solutions, one of the affected companies, reported Tuesday that its customer management portal and internal communications network had been rendered inaccessible since early morning. “Our technical teams are working round the clock, but we are dealing with a sophisticated breach,” spokesperson Tashi Dorji said. “We urge customers to bear with us as we restore services.”

The attack, described by officials as a ransomware incident, has not resulted in any reported outages to electricity supply as of midday, but billing, outage reporting, and maintenance scheduling services have been disrupted for thousands of customers. “We are unable to process bill payments or respond to new connection requests at this time,” Dorji added.

The Bhutan Electric Utilities Association called the incident “unprecedented” and said it is coordinating with the government’s Department of Information Technology and Telecom. “We are concerned about the potential for extended operational delays if systems are not restored soon,” said CEO Sonam Phuntsho.

Cybersecurity analyst Karma Wangdi noted that the attack highlights vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure. “This incident underscores the urgent need for enhanced cyber defenses in the sector,” Wangdi said.

The Department of Information Technology and Telecom has urged the public to stay informed through official channels as efforts to contain the attack continue.
